verdict.rationale: dltHub documents scheduled pipeline runs on its own managed infrastructure. You deploy with `dlthub deploy`, set schedules through a decorator-based Python API, chain pipelines, and monitor run logs, so recurring background automation is a first-party capability rather than a one-off run. The evidence is marketing and summary-level only, so depth and autonomy beyond scheduled runs are unproven. missing for 10: detailed docs on schedule configuration (cron or triggers, retries, failure handling), evidence that agents act autonomously beyond executing scheduled runs, independent or hands-on corroboration of background scheduling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Deploy your pipelines with a single `dlthub deploy` command. Schedule, refresh, backfill, and observe runs with a familiar decorator-based Python API.
teams schedule, backfill, and chain their pipelines with dltHub.
Schedule lineage-aware pipeline runs with agents, all in Python
Any engineer on your team can ship production data, with agents doing the work on infra we run. Every run is logged and auditable.
Use the dltHub CLI and the Web UI at app.dlthub.com to monitor pipeline health, inspect logs, and diagnose failures.
